main_text.p: tur,subijci,& cœlū esse motus principium duntaxat exprimit. Tametsi omnium, quæ oriuntur cœlum, prima est efficiens causa, non propterea ipsum largiri formas rebus ipsis consequitur. Est enim uniuersalis cau sa,quæ quidē omnibus rebus, in quas agit, semper est eadē, idemq; cunctis,quod uni-cuiq; seorsum tribuit. Propterea absq; pro-prio agente nihil definitum producere po-test. Postulat enim rerum natura,ut à singu-laribus,definitisq; causis singularia produ-cantur,quo effectui sua semper respondeat causa. Quare philosophorum omniū prin-ceps libro Physicorum secūdo, singularem effectum à singulari determinataque causa, ut & communem ab uniuersali procedere apertissime docet. Idcirco omnis genera-tio,quę actio est,proprio agenti ac definito accepta maximè est referenda: quandoqui-dem omnis actio circa particularia semper uersatur, quemadmodū Aristoteles primoCap.1. libro Diuinæ philosophiæ nos docet. Pro-inde sol,cū causa sit communis, perse nec planta sine planta,neq; ullum animal per-fectū absq; animali producere potest. Hac de causa philosophus libro secundo Scien-tiæ naturalis ait, solem & hominem gene-rare

page.notes: The printed text ends with a hyphenated line break "gene-/rare" completed at the line "rare". Some letters are faint: "consequitur" and "Aristoteles" are read with confidence; the spelling "singularem" in the original appears as printed. Possible printing errors left as printed: "Propterea absq;" and "superior" sentence structure ("sol,cū" with "perse nec"). The marginal note "Cap.1." is partly smudged; read as printed. Some words in the first line are cut at the page top edge.
